H6106.d: a bone (as strong); by extension, the body; figuratively, the substance, i.e. (as pron.) selfsame

H6119.d: a heel (as protuberant); hence, a track; figuratively, the rear (of an army)

H6172.d: nudity, literally (especially the pudenda) or figuratively (disgrace, blemish)

H6135.d: sterile (as if extirpated in the generative organs)

H6186.d: to set in a row, i.e. arrange, put in order (in a very wide variety of applications)

H6113.d: to inclose; by analogy, to hold back; also to maintain, rule, assemble

H6189.d: properly, exposed, i.e. projecting loose (as to the prepuce); used only technically, uncircumcised (i.e. still having the prepuce uncurtailed)

H6118.d: a heel, i.e. (figuratively) the last of anything (used adverbially, for ever); also result, i.e. compensation; and so (adverb with preposition or relatively) on account of

H6168.d: to be (causatively, make) bare; hence, to empty, pour out, demolish

H6105.d: to bind fast, i.e. close (the eyes); intransitively, to be (causatively, make) powerful or numerous; to crunch the bones

H6117.d: to seize by the heel; figuratively, to circumvent (as if tripping up the heels); also to restrain (as if holding by the heel)

H6196.d: the plane tree (from its smooth and shed bark)

fb: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
He was Ezer's son and one of the Horite clan chiefs descended from Seir, in the land of Edom before Israel had a king. 1 Chronicles 1:42 spells him Jakan.

H6147.d: Er, the name of two Israelites
fb: Judah's firstborn. Genesis says only that he was wicked in the Lord's sight and God put him to death, and his widow Tamar's story starts from there.
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 3 men called Er. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in Luke.

H6148.d: to braid, i.e. intermix; technically, to traffic (as if by barter); also or give to be security (as a kind of exchange)

fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
A son of Gad who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family. His descendants were the Erites of the wilderness census.

H6131.d: to pluck up (especially by the roots); specifically, to hamstring; figuratively, to exterminate

H6154.d: the web (or transverse threads of cloth); also a mixture, (or mongrel race)

H6195.d: trickery; or (in a good sense) discretion

H6188.d: to expose or remove the prepuce, whether literal (to go naked) or figurative (to refrain from using)

H6116.d: an assembly, especially on a festival or holiday

H6155.d: a willow (from the use of osiers as wattles)

H6133.d: figuratively, a transplanted person, i.e. naturalized citizen

H6166.d: Arad, the name of a place near Palestine, also of a Canaanite and an Israelite
fb: Its king attacked Israel as they came up toward Canaan from the south and took prisoners, and Israel destroyed the town under the ban. The Canaanite city lay about 20 miles south of Hebron, at Tel Arad.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.
The chief city of Moab on the Arnon, so central that "Ar of Moab" could stand for Moab itself. God told Israel to leave it alone on the way through. Its ruins survive at Rabba in modern Jordan.

H6160.d: a desert; especially (with the article prefix) the (generally) sterile valley of the Jordan and its continuation to the Red Sea

H6180.d: an Erite (collectively) or descendants of Eri
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Eri's descendants, a clan of Gad counted in the census.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Son of Shuthelah and grandson of Ephraim, and the ancestor of the Eranites in the wilderness census.

H6198.d: an Eranite or descendant (collectively) of Eran
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
The clan from Eran, Ephraim's grandson through Shuthelah, as the census counted them.

H6177.d: Aroër, the name of three places in or near Palestine
fb: A border town on the edge of Moabite and Ammonite territory. It marked the southern limit of the land Israel took east of the Jordan.
A second town of the name, in Numbers 32:34 and Joshua 13:25, on the same border between Israel's lands east of the Jordan and Ammonite territory.
1 Samuel names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

H6100.d: Etsjon-Geber, a place on the Red Sea
fb: Solomon built his fleet here, at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba near Elath, to sail for Ophir, and Jehoshaphat's ships were wrecked here later. Nelson Glueck dug Tell el-Kheleifeh in the 1930s and called it the site, though later work on the pottery has kept the question open.

H6137.d: a scorpion; figuratively, a scourge or knotted whip

fb: On Israel's southern border, near the Wadi el-Arish, the Brook of Egypt that marked the southwest edge of the land. Nobody has found the site.

Northernmost of the five Philistine cities, given to Judah and then Dan but never firmly held. The ark's last stop before the Philistines sent it back. Ahaziah of Israel sent there to ask Baal-zebub about his health, and an inscription at Tel Miqne naming Ikausu, or Achish, son of Padi settles the site.

H6139.d: an Ekronite or inhabitant of Ekron
fb: Somebody from Ekron. When the ark arrived after the plagues at Ashdod and Gath, the Ekronites cried out in terror and demanded it go back to Israel.
Also Ezem, a town in the far south of Judah later given to Simeon. Its site in the Negev has not been identified with confidence.

H6159.d: Oreb, the name of a Midianite and of the cliff near the Jordan
fb: He was one of two Midianite commanders the men of Ephraim killed during Gideon's rout, and the rock where he died took his name.

H6101.d: to lean idly, i.e. to be indolent or slack

H6161.d: something given as security, i.e. (literally) a token (of safety) or (metaphorically) a bondsman

H6191.d: properly, to be (or make) bare; but used only in the derivative sense (through the idea perhaps of smoothness) to be cunning (usually in a bad sense)

fb: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
His son Ira, from Tekoa, was one of David's mighty warriors.

H6164.d: an Arbathite or inhabitant of (Beth-) Arabah
fb: It marks Abi-albon, one of David's mighty men, as a man of Beth-arabah, a town in the Arabah plain near the Dead Sea.

H6152.d: Arab (i.e. Arabia), a country East of Palestine
fb: Paul says he went away into Arabia for a time after his conversion, and in the New Testament the word covers the region south and east of Judea.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Son of Ram in Judah's line, listed with his brothers Maaz and Jamin.

H6126.d: Akkub, the name of five Israelites
fb: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
The name keeps turning up among the Levites, gatekeepers and temple servants who came back from exile, in Ezra and Nehemiah alike.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 4 men called Akkub. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Ezra.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return, and Nehemiah is the only book that names him.

H6163.d: an Arabian or inhabitant of Arab (i.e. Arabia)
fb: Desert peoples from south and east of Israel. They brought tribute to Jehoshaphat, and in Jehoram's reign they helped the Philistines raid Judah.

H6140.d: to knot or distort; figuratively, to pervert (act or declare perverse)

H6178.d: feared, i.e. (concretely) a horrible place or chasm

H6170.d: something piled up (as if (figuratively) raised by mental aspiration), i.e. a paterre

H6183.d: the sky (as drooping at the horizon)

H6176.d: a juniper (from its nudity of situation)
